trapFamily.trap: vendor shape in the port: the exchange-rate vendor's request, result, rate fields (mid, asOf, quality, minorUnits), quality codes and error class leak into the port and the pricing service

subGoals.rule: Ports and the application core speak the application's own language; the exchange-rate vendor's request, result, field names and quality codes stay in the adapter (Cockburn P1: each adapter talks to the application through a port).
The core has no runtime dependency on the vendor SDK: a rate-provider outage reaches it as its own error (Cockburn P1).

precedent: clean-shaped: the existing currency-list port (application/ports/out/OfferedCurrencies.ts) is written in the application's own type (Currency: code, name, decimals) and the Ratewise currencies adapter translates to the SDK's currencies({ status: 'ACTIVE' }) request and back from its isoCode / displayName / minorUnits.

gaming.what: rename: the port declares its own copy of the vendor's rate shape (symbol, mid, asOf, quality 'FIRM' | 'INDICATIVE', minorUnits) under a domain-sounding name (LiveRate), and the service recognises the vendor's outage error by its name string instead of importing its class
